key_insight: AdsNet predicts adsorption energies directly from local atomic environments, combining geometric sensitivity with computation that does not scale with total system size.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate catalyst screening and local interface relaxation without evaluating a full-system machine-learning potential.
method: Build a cutoff-based graph of adsorbate atoms and nearby surface atoms.
Use equivariant message passing with scalar and vector features to predict energy and per-atom contributions.
Obtain forces by automatic differentiation for projected gradient descent relaxation with adaptive line search.
evidence_signal: Trained on 33,920 DFT structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates, AdsNet reports energy RMSE of 0.032 eV and force RMSE of 0.047 eV/Å.
watch_item: A local cutoff may omit longer-range surface effects; accuracy on unseen chemistries and surfaces requires validation beyond the reported dataset.
paper_title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
